fixtures.preview: United host Bournemouth on Sunday (1am Monday Sydney), four days after a 4-1 Champions League loss at Como, with Michael Carrick's side winless in seven.
talking_points: United are seven games without a win, and Carrick admitted on Friday that they have 'lost our way a little bit'.
Captain Bruno Fernandes questioned the tactics after Como, and Carrick would not rule out leaving him out on Sunday.
Leny Yoro is back from suspension and Ayden Heaven is over his illness; Lisandro Martínez and Marcus Rashford are fitness doubts.
Reported absentees are Šeško, Mainoo, Shaw, Dorgu and Ugarte; Matthijs de Ligt returned at Como.

fixtures.preview: A 12:30pm UK trip to Stamford Bridge on Saturday 31 October.
Matchday 4 of the Champions League league phase brings Roma to Old Trafford.
A Sunday 4:30pm UK home game against Aston Villa, picked for TV.
The trip to Anfield is set for Sunday 22 November at 4:30pm UK time, live on Sky Sports in the UK.
A Sunday 3pm home game in round 2, part of a double-header with Sydney FC Women v Melbourne City at 5:45pm.
talking_points: Sydney opened with a 0-0 derby draw against Western Sydney that produced only one shot on target.
It's the 65th meeting: Sydney lead 28-22 with 14 draws, but Adelaide won the last two.
Jake Hollman has a knock and Jacob Farrell is out; Akol Akon may start after an impact off the bench.
Adelaide's round 1 game was postponed for AFC competition; Bart Vriends is injured and new signing Brody Burkitt replaces Luka Jovanovic.

fixtures.preview: A 5pm Halloween game in round 3 at AAMI Park, Melbourne City's home opener against last season's Grand Final opponents.
A Friday-night home game against the Mariners.
An away trip to Brisbane Roar in round 5, 6:40pm Brisbane time (7:40pm Sydney).
The Big Blue at Allianz Stadium on Sunday 6 December at 5pm.

big_matches.title: Barcelona v Real Madrid (El Clásico)
big_matches.why: First Clásico of the season at Camp Nou, with Barcelona top of LaLiga and Real Madrid third (Mon 26 Oct, 7am Sydney).
talking_points: Barcelona lead LaLiga and have scored 39 goals in nine matches; Madrid, third, have 23.
Barcelona have won six of the last seven Clásicos in all competitions.
Vinícius Júnior is banned, and Barcelona are without Olmo and Raphinha (thigh).
Kylian Mbappé has won only one of six meetings with Barcelona.

notes: Many sites blocked access (HTTP 403) or returned stale results, so several sections are shorter than their limits rather than padded.

Man Utd: team news is from Stretty News' report of Carrick's Friday press conference (24 Oct); ESPN's article wouldn't load and some injury statuses differ between outlets. I couldn't open manutd.com, so kick-off times come from the Premier League and UEFA pages. Stan Sport is listed as showing all 380 Premier League games and the Champions League (football360, UEFA); I didn't see per-match listings.

Sydney FC: fixtures were confirmed against club and A-Leagues pages, but broadcasters aren't confirmed per match; Paramount+ is named as an A-Leagues broadcast partner. Sydney FC's Adelaide team news is from a tips site and isn't final.

Big matches: Stan Sport is listed as the Champions League broadcaster and for all three Wallabies November Tests (rugby.com.au). Only the Clásico has a match-specific beIN listing. I didn't find confirmed talking points for the non-Clásico football games, so they have none.

Live sport: Kings v Phoenix has no published start time. No rugby union or tennis in Sydney in the next 4 weeks was found, and the WNBL fixture page didn't confirm Sydney Flames dates, so they're omitted.
Local: school events come from the downloaded Term 4 calendars and Week 2 updates. Nothing was found for the other school, and no current South Eveleigh events page could be opened.

Not found: matcha pop-ups in Sydney, junior parkrun or kids' fun runs near home, Pokémon/Minecraft/Roblox events, children's author talks, and confirmed sports-gear sales (Rebel's boots sale ended 11 Oct).

Groceries: Woolworths and Coles half-price lists weren't accessible, so most items have no was-price and there are no fresh fruit, meat or egg specials. Aldi's tuna runs to 30 Nov; the other items end 27 Oct, and Aldi's next-week specials start 28 Oct.
Horizon: Rugby World Cup, Australian Open, SCG cricket, Asian Cup, Women's World Cup and Pokémon were re-checked this run.
